title: Miami's Malachi Toney expected to undergo surgery after injuring ankle in practice - CBS Sports
description: There is hope within the program that Toney's injury won't be season-ending
body:
There is hope within the program that Toney's injury won't be season-ending

        The No. 1 Miami Hurricanes got some concerning injury news on Wednesday when star receiver Malachi Toney suffered an ankle injury in practice. Sources told CBS Sports' Matt Zenitz that Toney suffered a high-ankle sprain and is expected to undergo surgery, but there is hope within the program that Toney will be back in time for a potential College Football Playoff run.Toney is the Hurricanes' biggest offensive weapon with 73 catches, 1,027 yards and 13 touchdowns this season, and his production for the nation's top team has made him one of the Heisman Trophy favorites alongside his quarterback, Darian Mensah. Losing Toney the week of Miami's biggest game would be a disaster for the Hurricanes, as the Miami offense looks for ways to create explosive plays against a talented Notre Dame defense. Toney's importance to the Miami offenseLast year's win over Notre Dame was Toney's breakout performance as a freshman, as he caught six passes for 82 yards and one touchdown in Miami's 27-24 victory to open the season. Toney is the top threat the Irish were going to have to game-plan and account for with multiple defenders, and any losing his ability to get downfield and move in space is a significant loss for Miami. 
Toney accounts for 35.1% of Miami's receptions, 38.6% of receiving yards and 46.4% of receiving touchdowns this season. Cooper Barkate is second on the team in all of those categories with 28 catches for 372 yards and four touchdowns, and while talented, doesn't provide the same dynamic as Toney.The Hurricanes use Toney in myriad ways, and his ability to move around formations and alignments allows Shannon Dawson to attack different soft spots of defenses and prevents easy adjustments to what Miami is doing because of their variation. With Toney out, it allows the defense to focus more on slowing down Miami's run game. The Hurricanes are 21st in the country in rushing offense at 202.5 yards per game and are 10th in yards per attempt at 5.49. Mark Fletcher Jr. and Javian Mallory make up one of the nation's best running back tandems, but they're made all the more effective by the respect defenses have to give to the big-play threat the passing game always presents when Toney is on the field. 
Notre Dame's defense figured to face the difficult choice of sending more bodies into the box to slow the run or keep help over the top to prevent Toney from getting loose. The ripple effects extend well beyond the Hurricanes' passing game. Heisman Trophy implicationsBeyond the impact Toney's injury will have on Miami's biggest game of the season, Saturday's game against Notre Dame figured to be Toney (and Mensah's) best opportunity to author a Heisman moment on a big national stage. Toney was second in the Heisman Trophy odds coming into the week at +290 at FanDuel Sportsbook -- only trailing Mensah at +170. After the initial injury news was reported on Wednesday, Toney dropped to +800 and after word broke he would have surgery he was off the board entirely. Toney's injury could also impact Darian Mensah's Heisman chances, as his passing productivity would likely take a hit if his best receiver can't play or is limited. 
As a result, Ohio State receiver Jeremiah Smith is back to the top spot in the odds at +160, Mensah is back to +165, and Notre Dame quarterback CJ Carr jumps to +550 in third as the Irish have moved out to a 7.5-point favorite over the Hurricanes. CBS Sports will continue to provide updates on Toney's status as the week progresses and more information becomes available.

body:
The 2026 NFL season is at the halfway point, Week 9, so that means some of the top players who have dealt with long-term injuries are ready to begin their returns to action. Green Bay Packers coach Matt LaFleur told reporters that Micah Parsons' 21-day practice window to return from the torn ACL and torn meniscus is now open. That means Parsons will begin practicing with the Packers for the first time this season, with the goal of returning for the Thanksgiving week game against the Los Angeles Rams."He put a lot of effort and work into this. Having him out there will be a big boost for our team," LaFleur said, via ESPN.LaFleur also indicated Parsons will begin practicing as a limited participant in individual position drills while ramping him up to be full throttle in a couple of weeks. 
The New Orleans Saints could also get a key piece of theirs back as well: 2026 eighth overall pick wide receiver Jordyn Tyson. The rookie out of Arizona State dealt with hamstring issues in college, which have delayed his NFL debut. However, New Orleans Football Network reported Tyson will return to practice.While that is positive news for the Packers and Saints, many injury situations aren't as optimistic in Week 9. The Rams got bad news on Jaylen Watson on Wednesday, with the cornerback requiring season-ending shoulder surgery. He missed a game earlier this year after dislocating the shoulder and reaggravated the injury in last week's game against the Chargers.
"That's a big blow ... He's been such a stud for us. body:
Are the Bears the best team in the NFC? Our latest playoff projection answers that question
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 4, 2026
                            
                    at
    3:47 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            9 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        With the NFL season heading into its halfway point this week, I have some good news for everyone: All 32 teams are still mathematically alive to make the playoffs. And yes, that means even the Titans and Chargers could still make the postseason. I'm guessing they won't, but they could, and that's what matters here.Heading into Week 9, this is when we finally start to see the contenders separate themselves from the pretenders. But who are the real contenders? Who's actually going to make the playoffs? Glad you asked. To help us figure that out, we had our analytics expert, Stephen Oh, simulate the rest of the 2026 season. There are 151 games left on the regular-season schedule, along with 13 playoff games, and Oh simulated all of them. Not only did he project all eight division winners and the 14 playoff teams, but he also crowned a Super Bowl champion.  With that in mind, let's get to the projections. And just as a reminder, we're projecting what the NFL playoff field will look like at the end of the season. This is NOT the current playoff standings.       
     Projected AFC playoff field     The AFC playoff projection underwent some massive changes this week. The Broncos turned the AFC West upside down with their win over the Chiefs. Thanks to that victory, our model now projects that Denver ends up winning the division title for the second straight year. Here's the projected AFC playoff field (with each team's current record):      1. Bills (6-1) -- AFC East champion      2. Jaguars (5-2) -- AFC South champion      3. Broncos (6-2) -- AFC West champion      4. Bengals (5-2) -- AFC North champion      5. Chiefs (5-2)      6. Steelers (6-2)      7. Patriots (5-3)  JUST MISSED: Texans (2-5), Browns (5-3) If the Broncos win the AFC West, the Chiefs will enter the playoffs as a wild-card team, which has never happened in Patrick Mahomes' career. Since he took over the starting job in 2018, the Chiefs have made the playoffs a total of seven times, and all of those came after a season where Kansas City won the division. The Chiefs have been so good with Mahomes that they've NEVER played a road game in the wild card round with him at quarterback, but we could see that happen this year.
       Projected NFC playoff field       For the third time this season, we have a new team projected to win the NFC North. The Bears have taken over the top spot after their dominating win over the Seahawks on Monday night. Over the past eight weeks, we've seen the Vikings and Lions both projected to win the division, but heading into Week 9, our computer likes Da' Bears.   Here's the projected NFC playoff field (with each team's current record):      1. 49ers (6-1) -- NFC West champion      2. Bears (6-2) -- NFC North champion      3. Giants (4-2-1) -- NFC East champion      4. Buccaneers (3-5) -- NFC South champion      5. Vikings (6-1)      6. Lions (5-2)      7. Seahawks (4-4)   JUST MISSED: Packers (5-3), Rams (4-4) For the first time in NFL history, we could have a situation where TWO teams win their division despite not being over .500. Right now, our projection has the Giants winning the NFC East with a record of 8-8-1 and the Buccaneers winning the NFC South at 8-9. The Bucs started the season 0-4, but our computer loves them after watching Tampa Bay destroy two division rivals -- the Panthers and Falcons -- in consecutive weeks. 
There have been seasons where two teams have gotten in the playoffs at .500 or worse, but it's always involved at least one wild card team. For instance, the Commanders won the NFC East with a 7-9 record in 2020 while the Bears got in as a wild card team with an 8-8 record. However, there has never been a situation where two divisional winners both finish .500 or worse. If that happens, the biggest losers will be the Packers and Rams, both being projected to miss the playoffs despite finishing above .500.        Wild card round       AFC       (2) Jaguars 27-20 over (7) Patriots. The last time these two teams met in the postseason, the Jags lost a controversial game in the AFC Championship. This time around, the Jags get their revenge. Jacksonville beat the Patriots 35-6 back in Week 3, and although this game is much closer, the Jags still get the win.     (3) Broncos 21-19 over (6) Steelers. The last time the Broncos won the Super Bowl back in 2015, they started their playoff run with a win over the Steelers, so this could start to feel like deja vu for fans in Denver. These two teams will actually face each other on Black Friday, so we'll get to see them battle in the regular season before a possible playoff game in January.  (4) Bengals 26-25 over (5) Chiefs. If there's one quarterback who has had some major success against Patrick Mahomes, it's Joe Burrow. Not only did he lead the Bengals to a win in the 2021 AFC title game, but Burrow is 2-0 all-time against the Chiefs at home, and he continues that streak with another win here. NFC       (2) Bears 24-21 over (7) Seahawks. These two teams just met on Monday night with the Bears destroying the Seahawks on the road in Seattle. This time around, the Seahawks keep it closer, but they can't quite figure out how to stop Ben Johnson's offense. (6) Lions 29-23 over (3) Giants. The Lions have never won a road playoff game in the Super Bowl era (0-12), but they end that drought here with a win against an overmatched Giants team.       (4) Buccaneers 21-17 over (5) Vikings. The Buccaneers make history in this game by becoming the first NFC team ever to overcome a 0-4 start to make the playoffs. The Bucs then use their strong rushing attack to run over Minnesota's defense. With the loss, the Vikings' 6-0 start goes to waste, and Minnesota is forced to spend another offseason looking for a quarterback. And now, we're down to our final eight teams.               Divisional round       AFC       (1) Bills 34-24 over (4) Bengals. The Bills come out on fire after their bye week and knock off the Bengals in what would be the team's first playoff game at their new stadium. This would definitely be an interesting matchup, and that's because Joe Burrow is 2-1 all-time against Josh Allen. (2) Jaguars 21-19 over (3) Broncos. The Jaguars' first divisional playoff win ever came back in 1996 against the Broncos, and history repeats itself here with the Jaguars knocking off Denver again. This game ends up as a back-and-forth thriller that's decided by a Cam Little field goal late in the fourth quarter. NFC       (1) 49ers 28-27 over (6) Lions. Three years ago, the Lions blew a 24-7 lead against the 49ers in the NFC title game. They finally get their shot at revenge here, but they come up short. Brock Purdy out-duels Jared Goff and ends up leading the 49ers to their fifth NFC title game over the past eight seasons. (2) Bears 28-19 over (4) Buccaneers. These two teams are actually playing THIS WEEK on Sunday night in Chicago, so we'll be getting a possible preview of what a playoff game might look like. The Bucs' defense has been strong this season, but in our playoff game, it can't slow down Caleb Williams and the Bears offense. With a win here, the Bears advance to their first NFC title game since 2010. If you're scoring at home, we are now down to four teams: Two teams that have never won a Super Bowl (Bills and Jaguars) and two teams that haven't won a Super Bowl in over 30 years. The 49ers' last title came in 1994, while the Bears haven't won a Lombardi Trophy since 1985, when they won their first and only Super Bowl.        Conference title games       AFC Championship       (1) Bills 28-24 over (2) Jaguars. Last year, the Jaguars' season ended with a painful playoff loss to the Bills, and unfortunately for Jacksonville, they lost to Buffalo for the second straight year. With Josh Allen aiming to get to his first Super Bowl, he takes over the game and leads the Bills to a tight win. NFC Championship       (2) Bears 26-24 over (1) 49ers. With two offensive gurus going at it in Kyle Shanahan and Ben Johnson, this game could come down to who plays better defense, and right now, the Bears have the advantage on that side of the ball. The Bears' acquisition of Jeffery Simmons ends up as the move that puts them over the top as Chicago's defense comes up with several big plays in a wild road win. These two storied franchises have only met twice ever in the NFC title game (1984, 1988), and the 49ers have won both times, but Chicago finally gets its revenge.        Super Bowl LXI at SoFi Stadium       (1) Bills 27-26 over (1) Bears. If these two teams end up in the Super Bowl, it will definitely be a wild week in Los Angeles. Bills fans would show up with their folding tables, and Bears fans would Super Bowl shuffle from Chicago all the way to LA while wearing their Ditka mustaches to honor Da' Coach, who led the Bears to their only Super Bowl win back in 1985. Unfortunately for the Bears, they don't have that same 1985 defense to stop Josh Allen. The Bills quarterback wills his team to a win, and the city of Buffalo celebrates by having everyone jump through a flaming folding table. Joe Brady becomes just the third coach this century to lead his team to a Super Bowl win in his first year on the job. DJ Moore gets revenge on his old team by having a huge game. As for Allen, he finally gets the Super Bowl monkey off his back, and Bills fans end up holding a parade that runs all the way from Los Angeles to Buffalo.  We've been doing a projection every week since the start of the season, and here's a look at the projected Super Bowl each week.      
Preseason prediction: Rams over RavensAfter Week 1: Seahawks over RavensAfter Week 2: Seahawks over ChiefsAfter Week 3: Chiefs over Vikings After Week 4: Seahawks over ChiefsAfter Week 5: 49ers over ChiefsAfter Week 6: Chiefs over 49ersAfter Week 7: Bills over VikingsAfter Week 8: Bills over BearsAs you can see, this is the first time all season the Bears have been projected to make the Super Bowl. According to our model, the Bears have a 17.96% chance of winning the NFC, with the 49ers sitting right behind them at 16.99%. There are only two other teams higher than 10%: the Lions (15.92%) and Vikings (13.22%). As far as winning the Super Bowl, the computer says it's Bills or bust. Buffalo has a 15.5% chance of winning it all, which is a huge number when you consider that no other team is above 10%.

        Even as the confetti rained down from the rafters in Ballhalla, it was hard to believe that the Golden State Valkyries had actually won the 2026 WNBA title in just their second year of existence. No team in North American professional sports had ever become champions that fast, and the Valkyries did it without a single All-WNBA player -- a first in league history. "All it took was good people. That's it," Finals MVP Gabby Williams said. "All we heard last year, 'We don't have no stars, we don't have no talent.' Yeah right. We got good people. We got winners. We got people who are ready to put their bodies on the floor to win a game. They don't care about scoring. They just want to play defense and rebound and do whatever it takes. We built a beautiful culture here." 
        
            
                'I stayed patient': How Finals MVP Gabby Williams made history in Game 7 to fuel Valkyries to WNBA title
                
                    Jack Maloney                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
The Valkyries exceeded expectations in 2025 by becoming the first expansion team to make the playoffs in their inaugural season, but even after making Williams their marquee signing in free agency last offseason, no one expected them to be title contenders. If anything, their decision to punt on the 2026 WNBA Draft by trading the No. 8 pick (Flau'jae Johnson) for two second-rounders raised significant questions about their process. And when French center Iliana Rupert was ruled out for the season due to maternity leave, their frontcourt appeared extremely thin. And sure enough, the Valkyries got off to a middling start. As the midpoint of the season approached, the Valkyries were 10-7 and just 3-6 against teams that eventually made the playoffs. Everything changed after that point, ironically with three wins over the Atlanta Dream in the span of 11 days. Those victories were part of a nine-game winning streak that catapulted the Valkyries into the top half of the standings, where they would remain the rest of the way. They went 22-5 to close the season, and nearly chased down the Minnesota Lynx for the top seed. 
They did so on the back of one of the best defenses we have ever seen. The Valkyries' 99.1 defensive rating was more than four points per 100 possessions better than any other team, and they were second in opponent turnover rate (19.2%) and second in opponent true shooting (53.5%). Williams, who finished second to Angel Reese for Defensive Player of the Year, made the All-Defensive First Team, while Veronica Burton and Kiah Stokes were All-Defensive Second Team honorees. The Valkyries' defense, combined with excellent depth and complete buy-in from everyone in the organization, helped make up for an offense that could be downright disastrous. They didn't have a single player average even 15 points per game. Their 108.2 offensive rating was seventh in the league and the second-worst among playoff teams. They were dead last in field goal percentage (42.2%) and 13th in true shooting (54%). Their inability to generate reliable offense nearly ended their season in the first round. They trailed the Dallas Wings by 16 in the second half of their winner-take-all Game 3, and had to pull off a miraculous comeback to secure the first playoff series victory in franchise history. In the semifinals, they swept the reigning champion Las Vegas Aces despite shooting 36.4% from the field, and pulled off another dramatic second-half comeback in Game 3 before winning in overtime to complete the sweep. 
The Finals was more of the same. They held the Dream to eight points in the fourth quarter of Game 1 and pulled off another late comeback despite shooting 32.1%, the third-lowest field-goal percentage in a Finals win in league history. So it went the rest of the way. In their four Finals victories, the Valkyries scored 68, 67, 64 and 68 points, respectively. In Game 7, they trailed by nine in the second half and were stuck on 32 points late in the third before Williams took over. She scored 28 of her 30 points -- tied for the most in a winner-take-all game in Finals history -- in the second half, and hit the go-ahead 3-pointer with just over two minutes to play. "[Coach Natalie Nakase] told me to stay patient. I trust her with my life," Williams said when asked what flipped in the second half of Game 7. "I stayed patient. I trusted her. She said, 'Stay patient, stay patient. The game is going to open up for you.' And it did."
"It's what we did all year," Williams added. "Just trust each other."
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Season at a glanceRecord: 32-12 (No. 2 seed)Offensive rating: 108.2 (7th)Defensive rating: 99.1 (1st)Net rating: Plus-9.1 (1st)Biggest strength: DefenseThe Valkyries were one of the best defensive teams ever. They had high-end defensive talent in Williams, Burton, and Stokes, and an array of big, physical, and versatile wing players they could cycle through to maintain a high level of intensity throughout each game and the entire season. They led the league in defensive rating by a wide margin, forced turnovers at a high rate and shut down the paint. Remarkably, they held opponents to just 14 restricted-area attempts per game, 61.4% shooting on those attempts, and 31.1 points in the paint per game. Those marks all led the league.  
        
            
                Way-too-early 2027 WNBA Power Rankings: Valkyries on top; Fever, Lynx, Liberty have major offseason questions
                
                    Jack Maloney                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
Biggest weakness: ScoringOn the flip side, finding consistent offense was a major issue for the Valkyries. They launched a league-record 30.3 3-point attempts per game, and when the 3s were falling, they could really pile up some points. But when they weren't, the Valkyries didn't really have any answers. In addition to their inefficient shooting, the Valkyries were last in restricted area attempts per game (14) and 12th in free throw rate (0.271), and Williams' 14.4 points per game were the second-fewest by any team's leading scorer. Key free agentsKayla Thornton (Unrestricted)Tiffany Hayes (Unrestricted)Cecilia Zandalasini (Restricted)Kaitlyn Chen (Reserved)Biggest question: Can they sign a max free agent?Weeks after the Valkyries traded the No. 8 pick on draft night, general manager Ohemaa Nyanin said the deal was made to maintain salary cap flexibility. 
"We thought we had the opportunity to potentially sign another athlete," Nyanin said at the team's media day. "My job is to make sure we maintain an understanding of what's happening today and then what could happen in the future. So the flexibility that is needed to really be able to withstand whatever could happen in the future is something I hold near and dear to me."There were plenty of rumors, particularly surrounding Napheesa Collier, but the Valkyries did not sign another max free agent alongside Williams. Now, after winning the title anyway, they will have significant cap space this winter. The official salary cap number for 2027 remains unclear due to the new revenue-sharing model, but it should be upwards of the $7 million it was in 2026. The Valkyries only have $3.2 million in guaranteed money on the books for 2027.Nyanin could very easily sign a max free agent and still have enough flexibility to fill out the rest of the roster. And there are a number of big names on the market this year, including Collier, Jackie Young, Kelsey Mitchell and Kelsey Plum. 

        
            
                WNBA free agency rankings: 10 best players available, from Napheesa Collier to Sophie Cunningham
                
                    Jack Maloney                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
Collier would be the most natural fit. She's one of the most efficient scorers in the league and would provide a major boost to the Valkyries' offense without harming their defensive structure. In fact, the former Defensive Player of the Year could make the Valkyries even better on that side of the ball. Young isn't on Collier's level as a defender, but she's not a negative on that end either, and would give the Valkyries an elite offensive talent. Mitchell and Plum are arguably even better than Young on the offensive end, but are such poor defenders that the Valkyries may not be interested, no matter how much they could fix their scoring woes. The Valkyries' commitment to doing things their way has to be commended, but achieving consistent playoff success in the years to come will be difficult without more help in the scoring department. This offseason represents a unique opportunity to add a star without sacrificing any members of their core, and Nyanin's comments prior to the season showed that they are interested in acquiring a big name. But can they?
The past six months have been an advertisement for the Valkyries' culture, their rabid fan base, and the organization's commitment to excellence. In a vacuum, any player would want to be a part of this group. But in that regard, could winning the title backfire? Some players, especially stars, may not want to join the reigning champs for fear of being seen as front-runners, but it's too early to say how free agents will react. If Nyanin can convince a star to come to the Bay Area, that would be bad news for the rest of the league.WNBA Draft outlookThe Valkyries have all of their own picks (Nos. 14, 29 and 44) in the 2027 WNBA Draft, but their first-round selection at No. 14 is the only one that really matters -- certainly for 2027. Of course, that's if the Valkyries even want to make a pick. They essentially punted on the draft last season when they traded the No. 8 pick (Flau'jae Johnson) for two second-round picks. 
If they want to keep the pick, a draft-and-stash option like French forward Aïnhoa Risacher could be an option. She's an unselfish, defense-minded player and wouldn't disrupt the team's current operations. Plus, they already have three French players on the roster.

title: 2026 NFL trade deadline tracker: Latest deals, grades as Jacoby Brissett heads to Baltimore - CBS Sports
description: Track every completed deal before the Nov. 10 deadline, including Chicago's blockbuster addition of Jeffery Simmo
body:
Track every completed deal before the Nov. 10 deadline, including Chicago's blockbuster addition of Jeffery Simmons and the Colts' trades of Quenton Nelson and DeForest Buckner
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 4, 2026
                            
                    at
    3:47 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            9 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        A steady stream of blockbuster moves in advance of the 2026 NFL trade deadline redistributed some of the league's top talent at numerous positions. Even more impactful transactions could be on the way before Nov. 10, but in the meantime, the Chicago Bears are the biggest winners of the deadline thus far with their highly fruitful acquisition of Jeffery Simmons, while the Indianapolis Colts emerged as the most aggressive sellers in dealing Quenton Nelson and DeForest Buckner.Trade watch continues for a myriad of stars on struggling teams, including Jonathan Taylor, Khalil Mack, George Pickens and others. At the same time, teams battling for position at the front of the postseason race must decide how much to invest in those standouts who are available on the trade market.There is only one more week of games until the trade deadline, so this year's contenders and pretenders are about as clear as they will be before it is too late to buy and sell. It is safe to expect a flurry of moves in the coming days as those franchises gear up for the home stretch or look ahead to the future.Below is every in-season trade ahead of the NFL's 2026 deadline.Nov. 4: Ravens add another QB amid injury crisisRavens receive: Jacoby Brissett, TBDCardinals receive: TBDBaltimore has agreed to trade for Cardinals QB Jacoby Brissett, with a deal expected to be completed by this weekend. The compensation has not yet been announced. 
This was expected from the Ravens, because their quarterback situation went from bad to worse on Sunday. The highly anticipated return of starter Lamar Jackson lasted just one play. Jackson suffered a thumb injury and is now placed on IR. Tyler Huntley, who started in place of Jackson, took over but also went down. He is reportedly out for the season with a turf toe injury. The team relied on emergency third quarterback Joe Fagnano to finish the game, but he is also dealing with an ankle injury. In order to avoid the scare of a running back having to sub in as quarterback, they now have another option. Brissett has spent the last two seasons with the Cardinals. Oct. 29: Bears go all-in, acquire Jeffery SimmonsBears receive: Jeffery Simmons, 2028 fifth-round pickTitans receive: 2027 first-round pick, 2028 first-round pick, 2027 fourth-round pickIn giving up two first-rounders to secure a perennial All-Pro defensive tackle, the Bears went all-in and opened their Super Bowl contention window. The transaction paid immediate dividends when Simmons logged a sack and led the team with six tackles in his Chicago debut: A commanding 34-17 road win over the Seahawks. Mortgaging so much of their future first-round capital showed that the Bears trust their roster, as currently constructed, to compete at the top of the league, and Simmons is the kind of game-changing talent worth the steep price. His production in the pass rush and in run defense could help Chicago maximize its high-octane unit on the other side of the ball led by Caleb Williams.
This move sends the Titans deeper into their rebuild. Questions lie ahead about whether to stick with Cam Ward at quarterback, and with the first-round picks they acquired from dealing Simmons, there will be curiosity as to whether they will use one to land a new signal-caller. Regardless of how they use the picks, moving on from one of the greatest players in franchise history shows how bleak the present is in Tennessee and that all eyes are on the future.Trade grades:Bears: A- | Titans: C+Oct. 27: DeForest Buckner reunites with 49ers49ers receive: DeForest BucknerColts receive: 2027 fourth-round pickThe seemingly nonstop onslaught of injuries hit the 49ers' defensive line, resulting in CJ West landing on injured reserve with a bone chip in his knee and Alfred Collins being ruled out for the year with a torn patellar tendon. That heightened the need for immediate help in the trenches, so the 49ers brought Buckner back after his six-plus years in Indianapolis. The 49ers selected Buckner in the first round of the 2016 draft, and the best years of his prime came during his time in San Francisco, so this is a welcome return for someone the franchise remembers fondly. Buckner remains one of the NFL's top pass-rushing interior defensive linemen and will aid in the 49ers' Super Bowl push.Buckner's exit marked the second trade in one day for the slumping Colts, who are in the midst of tearing things down with multiple star players on the move and former general manager Chris Ballard out the door. There is an argument to be made that a Day 3 pick was an underwhelming return, but for a 32-year-old veteran on an expiring contract, the Colts were content to get at least something of value for a player who was likely to leave in free agency anyway. Buckner grew publicly frustrated with Indianapolis' struggles, which heightened the anticipation for his trade or an eventual departure at the end of his contract.
Trade grades:49ers: A | Colts: B+Oct. 27: Seahawks bolster offensive line with Quenton NelsonSeahawks receive: Quenton NelsonColts receive: 2027 third-round pick, 2028 fifth-round pickSeahawks general manager Jon Schneider is keen to make big-time moves ahead of the trade deadline. This is the fourth consecutive year in which Seattle made a play for an impactful midseason addition to its roster. Nelson is as stellar of an offensive lineman as there is on the trade market this year as a six-time All-Pro and should elevate a struggling Seahawks run game over the long term, even if his arrival did not deliver an immediate boost in the loss to the Bears in his debut. This is also a savvy transaction for the front office given that it stands to receive at least one compensatory third-round pick in 2027; trading a third-rounder for Nelson was thus an easy price to pay.The Colts got more in return for Nelson than they did for Buckner, which is to be expected considering his status as perhaps the top interior lineman in football. This is still a discount, though, and they remain without a first-round pick in either of the next two drafts. If they can use the third-rounder and next year's fifth-rounder to move up in the order, the trade deadline sale could prove more worthwhile.Trade grades:Seahawks: A | Colts: C+Oct. 11: Texans take a shot on Marvin Harrison Jr.Texans receive: Marvin Harrison Jr., 2027 seventh-round pickCardinals receive: 2027 second-round pick, 2027 sixth-round pickHarrison reunited with his college quarterback, C.J. Stroud, upon his arrival in Houston. Will that help him rekindle what has become a disappointing career? His first two games with the Texans were mostly underwhelming, but he did haul in a touchdown reception in Week 7 and could secure a more sizable target share as the team seeks for a go-to No. 2 option behind star pass-catcher Nico Collins. This is trending toward a lost season for the Texans, but they will have another year of control over Harrison and the option to pick up a fifth year in 2028. If they can mold him into the star he was supposed to become out of Ohio State, their passing game will be in excellent shape over the long haul.
Trading Harrison was an admission that he was a bust of a former first-round pick, but to get a second-rounder in the process and to upgrade with a Day 3 pick swap was about as good of a deal as the Cardinals could have landed. Harrison ran his course in the desert and was clearly a poor fit in Mike LaFleur's system, so maximizing his value in the trade was a big win for a team that is not going to contend for anything meaningful in 2026 anyway.Trade grades:Texans: C- | Cardinals: B+Oct. 7: Ravens land Cam JurgensRavens receive: Cam Jurgens, 2027 seventh-round pickEagles receive: 2028 second-round pick, 2027 fifth-round pickThe interior offensive line in Baltimore was a glaring issue last year and into the start of 2026. The Jurgens trade addressed that head-on. Not only did the Ravens find their long-term replacement for Tyler Linderbaum, who left in free agency, but the addition also allowed them to move Olaivavega Ioane from center back to right guard. The full benefits of this move may not show up until Lamar Jackson returns to action, whether that be later in 2026 or next season.On the Eagles' side, Jurgens' exit effectively marked the end of an era for a once-legendary offensive line that also saw longtime tackle Lane Johnson and legendary position coach Jeff Stoutland enter retirement. It is a turning of the page and one that netted a couple of draft picks for a franchise that now looks destined to rebuild following a six-game losing streak. Philadelphia had been playing Jurgens out of position, anyway.
Trade grades:Ravens: B+ | Eagles: B-Oct. 1: Joey Porter Jr. brings much-needed help to Cowboys defenseCowboys receive: Joey Porter Jr.Steelers receive: 2028 second-round pick, conditional 2027 sixth-round pick (vested)If Porter cannot fix the Cowboys' defense, then that unit might be broken beyond repair in 2026. Dallas made a splash to address its greatest weakness and has thus far seen the exact kind of individual impact it envisioned from the star cornerback, as he allowed a diminutive 39.6 passer rating and just three completions on 11 targets across his first four games with the team. Still, the unit around him is in shambles. And with Porter set to reach unrestricted free agency this offseason, this could be a one-year rental that fails to produce a postseason appearance.The Steelers made it clear that they were not going to shell out market-resetting money to keep Porter around on a long-term contract extension. By declining to meet his demands as he sat out the start of the season, they only had one viable option, which was to trade him. A first-round pick would have been the preferable return package, but Pittsburgh received the next-best thing with both a second-rounder and 2027 draft capital. That sixth-round pick in next year's draft already vested, as it was conditional upon Porter being active for just two games with the Cowboys.Trade grades:Cowboys: C | Steelers: B-Sept. 28: Giants find replacement QB in J.J. McCarthyGiants receive: J.J. McCarthyVikings receive: 2027 fifth-round pickThe torn knee ligaments Jaxson Dart sustained in Week 2 made the Giants desperate for quarterback help, because the rest of the roster remained talented enough to compete for the NFC East crown. The McCarthy acquisition at first came across as puzzling given his own struggles to stay healthy, his underwhelming play when available and the fact that New York already has a franchise quarterback and thus has little to gain from McCarthy potentially developing into a viable starter. But it has aged better than expected. McCarthy threw for 243 yards and a touchdown in the fourth quarter in Week 6, earned the starting job over Jameis Winston and promptly delivered a road win over the Texans to place the Giants in command of the division.
Getting anything in return for McCarthy after a disastrous start to his career was a win for the Vikings. He slipped all the way down to the third line of Minnesota's depth chart behind a couple of low-ceiling veterans in Kyler Murray and Carson Wentz and was clearly no longer part of the franchise's plans.Trade grades:Giants: C | Vikings: B+

title: Previewing a Week 10 that could reshape CFP race as biggest Saturday yet arrives - CBS Sports
description: In a season already defined by chaos, what will the most impactful regular-season weekend of the College Football
body:
In a season already defined by chaos, what will the most impactful regular-season weekend of the College Football Playoff era have in store?
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 4, 2026
                            
                    at
    3:30 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            7 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Why not call college football's upcoming slate the best-ever in the College Football Playoff era?That's not hyperbole, by the way. You'll need to keep the remote close on Saturday, when the offering provides a smorgasbord of first-round-caliber matchups and enough new data points to fill a spreadsheet for the selection committee next week, after its wild first set of rankings.This is what an expanded playoff promised -- more teams with meaningful games down the stretch carrying substantial weight within the SEC, Big Ten and Big 12 title discussions, along with Notre Dame's prove-it stage against No. 1 and unbeaten Miami. The Week 10 slate features six AP top-20 matchups, tying for the most ever in AP poll history for a single weekend. Half of college football's most meaningful games left will be played Saturday, making it arguably the most impactful single day of the CFP era, which dates back to 2014.
Before glancing at the narrative-setting games, we combed through the last 15 seasons of impactful November weekends that featured stunning results that made a significant impact on the following week's playoff rankings.
        
            
                Lane Kiffin, LSU enter defining November stretch as Alabama matchup carries CFP weight
                
                    Brad Crawford                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
How will Week 10's slate stack up with some of the best since 2014?Nov. 12, 2016: No. 2 Clemson, No. 3 Michigan and No. 4 Washington were all beaten, along with No. 8 Texas A&M and No. 9 Auburn. This was during the four-team era, which shifted Ohio State from No. 5 to No. 2 and dropped Washington to No. 6. Strangely, Michigan did not budge despite a loss to Iowa.Nov. 11, 2017: Rivalry games were unkind to top-ranked Georgia (which lost to Auburn) and third-ranked Notre Dame (which got clobbered by Miami). Both the Bulldogs and Fighting Irish fell out of the top 4 while the Hurricanes and Oklahoma moved in.Nov. 5, 2022: After the initial CFP rankings released that season, No. 1 Tennessee lost to Georgia, Notre Dame climbed past fourth-ranked Clemson, and LSU toppled sixth-ranked Alabama in overtime. Georgia moved to the No. 1 spot the following week, while TCU entered the top 4.Nov. 24-25, 2017: How often have CFP Nos. 1 and 2 lost during rivalry weekend? It happened here following second-ranked Miami's upset loss to Pittsburgh on Friday night and top-ranked Alabama's setback against Auburn the next day in the Iron Bowl. The Hurricanes dropped to No. 7 while the Crimson Tide fell to No. 4. One of those teams rebounded, reached the CFP and won the national championship under the legendary Nick Saban. Looking at Saturday's appetizing menu, parity could resurface, as it has weekly this fall, for contenders aiming to strengthen their grip on coveted seeds while battling opponents with a margin for error nearing zero.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    
                            
    
                                                
                    
    No. 9 BYU at No. 3 UtahStakes: Winner takes the driver's seat in the Big 12 Championship raceThere's nothing like a Holy War that means something nationally, and this one is particularly juiced up in Salt Lake City. BYU's trip to Utah could help determine whether the conference's three-bid playoff ambition remains realistic or deteriorates should the Utes win. That would put BYU's best-case finish at 10-2, falling short of a berth in the conference title game if Utah and Texas Tech win out. Cincinnati was supposed to be a worthy adversary for the Utes last time out, but Utah steamrolled the Bearcats after taking out the Red Raiders. 

                            
    
                                                
                    
    
                            
    
                                                
                    
    No. 8 UCLA at MinnesotaStakes: Bruins' first loss would create a three-way tie for first in the Big TenThe best way UCLA can prove the non-believers wrong is to keep winning. Nothing's been pretty the last few weeks for one of college football's three remaining unbeatens, but the Bruins are getting it done. Offensive efficiency is ranked 48th nationally right now against a favorable schedule without Nico Iamaleava at quarterback following his season-ending injury, and that's part of the reason many have tried to poke holes in this unblemished start. However, UCLA has allowed just 35 total points over its last five games, and this weekend's opponent has been offensively challenged at times, scoring only a couple of touchdowns in the season's second half. Keep it moving, Bruins -- however that may look.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    
                            
    
                                                
                    
    No. 7 Texas at No. 18 MissouriStakes: Longhorns aim for a nation-leading fourth win against ranked opponentsEli Drinkwitz must love this situation for the Tigers. No one has mentioned Missouri in the CFP race, but that'll change if it takes out the Longhorns this weekend. Texas isn't upset-proof by any means after losing at home to Florida a few weeks back and stubbing its toe against Oklahoma in Red River. Luckily for Steve Sarkisian and Arch Manning, the wins look good (Ohio State, Tennessee, Ole Miss) and they're also aging well down the stretch. Texas will have the best three-loss resume of any at-large team if the Longhorns take three of their final four games.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    
                            
    
                                                
                    
    No. 5 Alabama at No. 14 LSUStakes: Without a ranked win thus far, Lane Kiffin's back is against the CFP wall
We're not quite ready to call this one a CFP elimination game in the SEC, but it's close. Should both of these teams finish 9-3 and be within the expected SEC logjam of squads with the same record, the winner here has a leg up. And for LSU, holding potential losses to Ole Miss, Kentucky and Alabama -- all three of which could end with the same record -- that would be all she wrote. The first of three straight games against top-15 opponents for the Tigers; win two and we think LSU will be in as one of the final at-large selections. The Crimson Tide have two ranked wins (Kentucky, South Carolina), but don't have that signature victory yet. This would be it in Baton Rouge to solidify a spot as long as Alabama wins out from there.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    
                            
    
                                                
                    
    No. 23 Oregon at No. 12 Ohio StateStakes: A Buckeyes loss would complicate their path to a CFP at-large berthSo much for style points. Oregon's visit to Columbus gives the two-loss Buckeyes an opportunity to steady themselves after the USC debacle, but another stumble would leave their CFP hopes dependent on considerable help from others -- and that's not where Ryan Day wants to be on Sunday. The Ducks have endured their own disappointing season, going from top-5 to unranked, but they still have enough ability to make this a nervous matchup inside the Horseshoe if Dylan Raiola plays as well as he did last week against Northwestern. Win, and Ohio State stays where it wants to be in the national picture. Lose, and the conversation shifts to the bubble for the Buckeyes.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    
                            
    
                                                
                    
    No. 6 Kentucky at No. 13 TennesseeStakes: Vols look to snap the Wildcats' six-game winning streak and enter the top 10
Tennessee has more to lose here despite Kentucky being the higher-ranked -- and hotter -- team. This home game carries the urgency of a playoff elimination game for Tennessee, especially with LSU still waiting on the schedule and only one ranked win (Alabama) so far. Another defeat would leave the Vols, if they win out, asking the selection committee to overlook three losses while comparing its résumé against a crowded group of at-large contenders. Kentucky's stakes are significant, too, but the Wildcats still have favorable games against Missouri, Florida and Louisville to navigate after leaving Knoxville. If Kentucky does pull this one off as a betting underdog for its seventh consecutive win, Will Stein is all but guaranteed the program's first CFP appearance unless the bottom falls out the final three games. Kentucky fans would be making reservations for the SEC Championship in Atlanta, too. For Tennessee, winning feels essential to keeping a realistic path to the bracket open in November.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    
                            
    
                                                
                    
    No. 2 Georgia at No. 10 Ole MissStakes: An Ole Miss win all but guarantees a CFP berth, while a loss could be fatal
The Rebels have wins over LSU and Missouri in their back pocket, but one that would really age well in the coming weeks is a victory over Georgia on Saturday. That's the only team with a winning record remaining for Ole Miss, which might not be in the 12-team field with a loss here and a 9-3 finish. This one's dangerous for Georgia because the guy playing quarterback for the Rebels has already thrashed this Glenn Schumann defense twice in his career. It was Trinidad Chambliss' late-game heroics that sent the Bulldogs home in the CFP quarterfinals last season, and he nearly beat Georgia between the hedges, too. Perhaps the most important factor will be the turnover battle and Pete Golding's defense doing what it can to frustrate Gunner Stockton and Georgia up front.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    
                            
    
                                                
                    
    No. 1 Miami at No. 11 Notre DameStakes: Unbeaten and top-ranked Hurricanes hope to make things uneasy for Fighting IrishTwo of college football's most efficient teams this season go head-to-head in South Bend for a matchup that should get millions of eyes Saturday night. How good is Notre Dame when the only ranked team the Fighting Irish played this season -- BYU -- beat them in October? The same question can be asked about the Hurricanes, who held off Wake Forest in September but have since played only two opponents with winning records. Miami needed double overtime to hold Florida State on Oct. 17 and nearly lost at North Carolina last week in a lookahead spot before this one. Notre Dame swatted its only common opponent (Tar Heels) a few weeks ago and should give Miami's explosive offense -- featuring the Heisman frontrunner at quarterback -- its toughest assignment up to this point.

title: Gianluigi Donnarumma was signed to be world's best shot-stopper, but at Manchester City, he's merely fine - CBS Sports
description: City compromised their possession philosophy to land an elite shot-stopper, but mounting mistakes show the Italia
body:
City compromised their possession philosophy to land an elite shot-stopper, but mounting mistakes show the Italian is failing to deliver on the trade-off
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 4, 2026
                            
                    at
    7:08 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            3 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Hard as it may be to believe or justify after events in Leipzig, there was a logic to Manchester City jettisoning their decade-long policy for goalkeeper recruitment last summer and signing Gianluigi Donnarumma. When your greatest defensive attribute is how your possession constricts your opponents from your third of the pitch then what you want from your No.1 is someone who can keep and progress the ball. Ederson is the dream. Even an aged Claudio Bravo is tolerable.That all changed when Rodri's anterior cruciate ligament went in September 2024. Suddenly Manchester City were unable to shut down the opposition, to block off the counter and keep the other team to hitting and hoping. Having allowed somewhere around seven and a half shots in each of the previous four seasons, City allowed 9.34 in 2024-25, 9.71 in 2025-26. Now that Enzo Maresca has taken the helm and concluded that Elliot Anderson is enough of a midfield, we are at 10.56 in the Premier League. In the Champions League, where so many of City's opponents know best how to play on the front foot, it is 11 shots allowed per game (that average isn't as warped by playing PSG as you think).If you're going to allow that much extra pressure on your goal, you want someone who can keep the ball out. In principle, Gianluigi Donnarumma is that guy, certainly if he is the player who carried Paris Saint-Germain through so many crucial moments and to their first Champions League title. But, of course, he isn't. 
                                                                    TruMedia
                                                            In Leipzig tonight, the outfield players managed to cover for their increasingly error-prone goalkeeper, Erling Haaland scoring a 13th goal in nine meetings with the Bundesliga side and earning a 3-2 win for City. Covering for Donnarumma was not something this team were able to do when he let Nicolas Jackson's shot through his gloves at Villa Park, nor when he got done by Desire Doue and Vitinha in PSG's heavy win at the Etihad.Those errors betrayed a 6ft 5in frame with the manoeuvrability and burst of an 18-wheeler. Donnarumma might still be just 27 years old but his movement in recent months betrays every one of his 12 years as a first-team player, 553 games on the clock and a lot of rubber burned off those tyres.
You could potentially add Antonio Nusa's goal, Leipzig's second equaliser, into the category of shots Donnarumma might have got down to quicker. It's a 0.2 xG shooting position, one that the Norwegian hit fiercely enough that its post-shot value was 0.65. In other words, Donnarumma would have been doing very well if he saved it. This is, however, Manchester City's goalkeeper, one recruited for his shot-stopping above all else. You're entitled to expect him to do very well.Especially when he was so cataclysmically clumsy for the first equaliser. Any goalkeeper's primary job is to protect his goal. In drifting three yards off his line when Riedle Baku was in a crossing position, Donnarumma was trying to take the easy way out. Again, a shot-stopper who is quicker to get down to the ball might have dealt with it. Certainly the Italian couldn't argue much that he had been unlucky; replays would suggest Baku saw the gap and hit it precisely.
Of course Donnarumma had had his moments earlier, a smart diving save denying Christoph Baumgartner's long-range strike. The same is true of this season and his City career as a whole. At his best, he has recovered that aura of his final months at PSG and across 56 games in the Premier League and Champions League, he has conceded six fewer goals than the post-shot xG value of the shots he has faced. In last season's Premier League he was one of the better pure shot-stoppers in the league; this time he is there or thereabouts.
As a whole, Donnarumma has been fine. It's just that he was not bought to be fine. If you're tolerating a goalkeeper who can't give you much at all in possession, it is because you want the best in the world at keeping the ball out. It seems like a long, long time since Donnarumma could lay claim to that moniker.

The Italian side managed to score nine goals away against Lens and are now fourth in the league phase standings

                How Como became a Champions League team: Unique model, ownership power, Cesc Fabregas lead impressive rise
                
                    Francesco Porzio                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
Only PSG, Real Madrid and Arsenal have done better than Como after four Champions League matchdays. If that's not enough, they have a better goal difference than Barcelona, Manchester City and Liverpool, and more points than Bayern Munich or their Serie A rivals Inter, AS Roma and Napoli. You must be surprised, especially after Cesc Fabregas and his team won 9-1 away at Lens, one of the greatest wins in the European history of Italian soccer. Well, you shouldn't be. This is the result of a long-term project with a clear vision, a talented roster and one of the best emerging coaches in Europe. Here's what to know about this exciting team.
The coach: Cesc FabregasThe Spanish head coach joined Como as a player before retiring. He also started his coaching career at the club, taking charge of the Under-23 side and making a name for himself in the country. In the three years since becoming first-team head coach, Fabregas has clinched promotion to Serie A, a 10th-place finish in his first top-flight season and then Champions League qualification in his second full season in Italy's top flight. Beyond the results, Como have consistently showcased a clear tactical identity built around attacking football and an intense high press, delivering some of the most entertaining performances the league has seen in recent years. Fabregas has a clear footballing philosophy built around specific principles, and he is determined to achieve results without compromising his vision of how the game should be played. So far, he has managed to do just that.Fabregas is able to deliver results on his own terms thanks to the club's backing, further strengthened by his position as a minority shareholder. When Inter wanted to hire him to replace Simone Inzaghi in the summer of 2025, the club and the coach agreed to continue together despite interest from multiple clubs. Como president Mirwan Suwarso has spoken multiple times about the possibility of Fabregas leaving one day, knowing more clubs will knock on their door. At the same time, even for a coach as talented as Fabregas, it will be difficult to find another place like Como, where his views and decisions are not only welcomed but concretely supported. There aren't many clubs like that.The best player: Nico Paz When it comes to the players, there are multiple examples of how Como work in the transfer market, but Argentine midfielder Nico Paz is probably the one that best fits the club's vision. In the summer of 2026, Como signed him permanently from Real Madrid for around €60 million, a club-record fee, and extended his contract on a long-term basis.
Paz first joined Como in the summer of 2024, when the Italian club agreed a permanent deal with Real Madrid worth €6 million. The Spanish giants wanted to keep control of the player, though, inserting a 50% sell-on clause and the right to match any offer from another club. They also had the right to re-sign Paz in each of the following three summer transfer windows, for €9 million in the first year, €10 million in the second and €11 million in the third. Two years later, when Como moved to make his stay permanent, they agreed a deal worth around €60 million, while Real Madrid retained the option to bring him back in the summer of 2027 for €80 million.
This isn't just about one club doing a deal with another. It's also about the will of a player who wanted to stay at Como despite having the chance to return to Real Madrid. That says a lot about the potential of the project, as Paz is not just a talented midfielder but also the new face of Argentina after Lionel Messi retired from the national team earlier this year. In his four Champions League games so far, Paz has delivered three goals, including a brace against Manchester United, and five assists.
In other places or contexts, we would assume both Fabregas and Paz were just waiting for a better offer before moving on. At Como, the situation is different. The club have a long-term project and a model that could keep both of them there for many years, building something special and competing for major honors. Winning trophies is no longer just an ambition. It's becoming the club's next objective, and nights like the one against Lens are proof of that.

title: Jacoby Brissett trade: Ravens strike deal for Cardinals QB amid injury crisis - CBS Sports
description: Baltimore is expected to acquire the veteran quarterback from Arizona after injuries to Lamar Jackson, Tyler Hunt
body:
Baltimore is expected to acquire the veteran quarterback from Arizona after injuries to Lamar Jackson, Tyler Huntley and Joe Fagnano decimated its depth chart
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 4, 2026
                            
                    at
    3:00 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            2 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        The Baltimore Ravens are adding another quarterback to lead a room that has been devastated by injuries, according to ESPN. Baltimore has agreed to trade for Arizona Cardinals quarterback Jacoby Brissett. The deal is expected to be completed this weekend, and compensation has not been finalized. Two-time NFL MVP Lamar Jackson suffered a thumb injury that required surgery on his first pass attempt against the Buffalo Bills on Sunday. It could potentially be a season-ending injury. Jackson's backup, Tyler Huntley, came in and suffered a season-ending turf toe injury, leaving undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano as the likely candidate to start the Ravens' Week 9 matchup against Trevor Lawrence and the Jacksonville Jaguars on Thursday night. However, he is also dealing with an ankle injury. Brissett has spent the past two seasons in Arizona. The Cardinals recently demoted him from starter to third-stringer after Gardner Minshew came in on Sunday, threw three touchdowns, and helped Arizona eliminate a 14-point deficit in the fourth quarter to defeat the Dallas Cowboys in overtime, 33-30. Brissett completed 10 of 23 passes for 119 yards and one interception before being replaced.Brissett, who turns 34 next month, has completed 63.3% of his passes for 1,719 yards, 10 touchdowns and seven interceptions in eight games this season. CBS Sports Research points out that his 75.6 yards per game to star tight end Trey McBride entering Week 8 were the most by a QB-TE combo since 1970 (min. 15 games). This is the second time he has been traded in his career, and the Ravens mark his seventh team.
While Brissett can't replace what Jackson brought to this Ravens offense, he is an experienced quarterback who has started 73 games (23-50) and thrown 86 more touchdowns than the rest of the Ravens' healthy quarterbacks combined. His 1.5% career interception percentage is also tied for second-lowest in NFL history behind Aaron Rodgers' 1.4%. Brissett is one of five quarterbacks in the past 365 days to throw for 4,000 yards and 25 touchdowns, joining a list that includes Drake Maye, Matthew Stafford, Jared Goff and Dak Prescott. He also upgrades his own situation. Over the last calendar year, the Cardinals have allowed 32.6 points per game -- which is four points higher than any other team in the NFL. The Ravens have allowed 10 points fewer per game (22.6) in that same span. 
Baltimore sits in the basement of the AFC North at 4-4, but hope a veteran under center can propel the Ravens to a playoff spot.

title: MLB rumors: The only Oriole not on the trading block, Rays' Drew Rasmussen plan and Astros add to manager hunt - CBS Sports
description: Here are the latest MLB trade and free agency rumors for Wednesday, Nov. 4
body:
Here are the latest MLB trade and free agency rumors for Wednesday, Nov. 4
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 4, 2026
                            
                    at
    2:49 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            3 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        The Brewers have now been World Series champions for just one week (minus a few hours) and they should still be basking in the glory for quite a while. As the offseason marches on, the next big date will be Nov. 17, when decisions on qualifying offers are due from the eight players who received one. In the meantime, the rumor mill should be ever-so-slowly churning. We'll round it up here. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Astros to interview Pujols for manager openingThe Houston Astros moved on from general manager Dana Brown in August and fired manager Joe Espada after the 2026 season. Newly hired general manager Randy Flores is now tasked with landing a new dugout boss, and a three-time MVP and future Hall of Famer is in the mix. The Astros will interview Albert Pujols for the manager job this week, per The Athletic.Pujols has long made it known that he desires to be an MLB manager. He recently interviewed for vacancies with the Padres and Angels (both last offseason) and he also managed the Dominican Republic in the World Baseball Classic this past spring. It should be further noted that Pujols is in the fourth year of a 10-year, $100 personal services contract with the Angels that was part of the mega-deal he signed with them as a player prior to the 2012 season as a player. 
Other known candidates for the Astros manager job are Rangers bench coach Luis Urueta and Yankees bench coach (not to mention former Tigers and Angels manager) Brad Ausmus. Former Astros third baseman Morgan Ensberg, the manager of the Triple-A Rays affiliate Durham Bulls, will also interview this week, according to MLB.com.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Orioles looking to deal for SP and OF helpThe Orioles are willing to listen to trade offers on any player other than Pete Alonso as they seek both rotation and outfield help, according to The Baltimore Banner. The  Orioles reportedly aren't "actively shopping" any players, but they are looking for upgrades at starting pitcher and outfielder and realize one of the ways that could happen is via a trade. Surely they wouldn't sell low on Gunnar Henderson, given his immense upside, so we can probably take him off the table unless some team makes it worth their while. There is a glut of infielders, though. With Alonso at first base and Henderson at short, they have Jackson Holliday, Christian Encarnacion-Strand, Jordan Westburg and Coby Mayo for two spots. Even using one of the four at designated hitter, it's easy to see where a deal could happen. 
Westburg and Encarnacion-Strand are under team control through 2029 while Holliday is controlled through 2030 and Mayo through 2031. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Rays want to keep RasmussenThe American League champion Rays recently picked up the $20 million club option on All-Star starting pitcher Drew Rasmussen. That would be a franchise-record salary for one player in a single season. It might seem odd to exercise an option and then deal a player to an outsider, but locking Rasmussen in for a one-year deal makes him an attractive trade candidate instead of just letting him walk in free agency, and this is how the Rays generally operate. We've seen it so many times: they get ahead of losing guys to free agency, sometimes even dealing them a year or two earlier. They've done it with Randy Arozarena, Isaac Paredes, Tyler Glasnow and even going back to franchise legends like David Price, Evan Longoria and Ben Zobrist. The Rays right now are saying they intend to keep Rasmussen for 2027."Not a declarative this, that, whatever, but I can sit here very confidently and say that every intention right now is thinking about Ras anchoring our rotation and how to make this team better going into next year," club president Erik Neander said on Tuesday, via the Tampa Bay Times.
If they want to contend again next year, it sure seems like they need Rasmussen, with Nick Martinez and Freddy Peralta off to free agency. That leaves Rasmussen atop the rotation, followed by Shane McClanahan, Griffin Jax, Ryan Pepiot and a bunch of question marks. There are questions attached to McClanahan, Jax and Pepiot too.

title: LIV Golf shutdown imminent? New financial backer pulls funding from fledging league - CBS Sports
description: BC Partners has reportedly walked away from its $300 million rescue plan due to a lack of player commitments
body:
BC Partners has reportedly walked away from its $300 million rescue plan due to a lack of player commitments
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 4, 2026
                            
                    at
    4:42 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            2 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Just over six months after losing its original financial backer, LIV Golf has reportedly seen its potential savior fall by the wayside as private capital firm BC Partners has decided to drop its bid to keep the league running. BC Partners had previously committed upwards of $300 million to keep LIV Golf afloat with the circuit aiming to reinvent itself in the wake of Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund deciding to no longer finance the upstart league that once aimed to put the PGA Tour out of business.While approximately 15 players had expressed interest in "LIV Golf 2.0," BC Partners decided to pull the funding it had originally committed in August, believing there are not enough golfers -- nor enough notable names -- attached to the project to keep the league viable, according to The Athletic and the Financial Times. The capital firm was expecting at least twice as many player commitments.LIV Golf now may have no choice but to liquidate its assets and shutter the league entirely.The PIF previously invested approximately $7 billion total to start LIV Golf, fund outsized player contracts (some of which reached nine figures) and keep the league running for five seasons. Once the PIF withdrew its funding, the league was forced to cancel two tournaments; it also failed to pay vendors and some of its players. LIV Golf filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection in September, promising to find a new backer and reimagine the league.
Nearly every major LIV Golf player has departed the league, including Jon Rahm, who reached a high-profile separation agreement with the circuit, Tyrrell Hatton and Sergio Garcia. Brooks Koepka previously took a lifeline by accepting penalties and returning to the PGA Tour ahead of the 2026 season, while Bryson DeChambeau recently stated that he was planning to see LIV Golf's new iteration through. Dustin Johnson, Cameron Smith and Joaquin Niemann are among other players whose contract situations are murky.Representatives for Rahm and other LIV Golf creditors are scheduled to appear at a hearing in New Jersey on Thursday, hoping to finalize their agreements. With LIV Golf now unfunded immediately ahead of its court date, it may choose to liquidate its assets and fold the league entirely.The PGA Tour has been hesitant to open additional pathways for former LIV Golf players to return, though some could regain their playing cards and compete in tournaments through traditional qualifying procedures.

title: Matthew Stafford's wife calls out NFL over apparent scheduling disadvantage given to Rams - CBS Sports
description: Los Angeles will play in the NFL's first-ever Thanksgiving Eve game, which doesn't give the Rams a true bye week
body:
Los Angeles will play in the NFL's first-ever Thanksgiving Eve game, which doesn't give the Rams a true bye week
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 4, 2026
                            
                    at
    4:27 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            2 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        For the first time ever, the NFL will play a game the night before Thanksgiving, with the Los Angeles Rams hosting the Green Bay Packers in a rare Wednesday matchup on Nov. 25 at 8 p.m. ET on Netflix. To make the game work on the schedule, both teams were essentially forced to sacrifice their bye week, and Kelly Stafford definitely isn't happy about that fact. The wife of Matthew Stafford took to social media this week to call out the NFL for putting the Rams at a scheduling disadvantage compared to the league's other teams. "Just curious to hear the thought process behind making the Rams the only team in the NFL without a true bye week," Kelly wrote on Instagram. "Because damn, after 18 years around this league, even I need a week off during the season...and I have never played a single snap."Normally, a team goes 14 days between games during a bye week, but the Rams will only be getting 10 days off. Here's what their schedule looks like in the lead-up to their Thanksgiving Eve showdown with the Packers: 
Week 10 (Nov. 15): at Cardinals (Sunday)Week 11 (Nov. 22): BYEWeek 12 (Nov. 25): Packers (Wednesday)Week 13 (Dec. 3): Chiefs (Thursday)The Packers will be in a similar situation, but they get a slightly more favorable schedule since they don't have to play on Thursday night in Week 13. Instead, the Packers will play on Sunday, Dec. 6, so Green Bay will play only one game over a 19-day period. They still won't have a full bye, but it's better than what the Rams have. Here's what Green Bay's schedule looks like in that same window: Week 10 (Nov. 15): Vikings (Sunday)Week 11 (Nov. 22): BYEWeek 12 (Nov. 25): at Rams (Wednesday)Week 13 (Dec. 6): at Saints (Sunday)
NFL teams look forward to the bye each year so they can rest and heal, but Rams and Packers players won't be getting the full week off in 2026. "I'm tired just watching from the stands," Kelly wrote. "Can't imagine how the guys feel."Kelly then ended things by asking the NFL to explain why the Rams got hosed over. 
"Anyway, feel free to leave that explanation right here," Stafford said. The Rams were given one of the wildest schedules in the NFL this year. Not only are they playing a Wednesday game, but they also have a Friday game against the Seahawks on Christmas Day. If the Rams end up playing a Saturday game, which could happen if they get flexed in Week 17 or Week 18, they'd become just the fourth team in 99 years to play a game on six different days of the week during a single season. The Rams have been the NFL's guinea pigs this year. They also played in the inaugural Australia game back in Week 1. Thanks to that trip, the Rams are scheduled to travel more than 34,000 miles this season, which is the second-most in the NFL. Although Kelly Stafford isn't happy about the Rams losing their bye week, the Rams will be home for Thanksgiving. That means they'll get to spend the holiday weekend with their families, so the team's odd schedule isn't a total loss.
